chunks: From him, from al-Naḍr, from Mūsā ibn Bakr, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

That two men from among the Muslims were in al-Kūfah. Then a man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and testified that he had seen them praying to an idol. So he said to him: “Woe to you, perhaps it was someone who resembled them to you.”

So he sent a man, and he looked at them while they were praying to an idol. Then they were brought, and he said to them, “Return [from this].” But they refused. So he dug for them a trench in the ground, kindled a fire, and cast them into it.

key_terms.خَدًّا: a trench or dug channel in the ground
key_terms.ٱرْجِعَا: return back; here meaning to recant and return to Islam

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام deal with idol-worship and apostasy after verifying the accusation?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام investigated a report of apostasy before acting, confirming the claim through verification. After the two men were found worshipping an idol and refused to recant, he carried out a severe punishment, reflecting the juridical treatment of manifest apostasy in this chapter.
